value: Supply: your troops carry limited ammo and refill it inside your supply area: around your buildings and Supply Depots, along the green supply lines on the roads (L shows them), or beside an Ammo Truck from your War Factory. Crater an enemy road or hunt its Ammo Trucks to starve the front.
Armor is thickest at the front: hits on a vehicle's side do 20% more damage, from behind 60% more. Flank them.
Infantry in woods or beside buildings take less damage. Fight from cover.
Firing downhill helps and firing uphill hurts. Take the high ground.
Infantry under heavy fire get suppressed: they shoot and move slower until it wears off.
Moving targets are harder to hit. Keep your vehicles moving under fire.
Capture oil derricks with infantry or vehicles for extra income.
Quarries and mines pay income, a captured Field Hospital heals your infantry nearby, and a power plant adds power: move infantry next to them to capture them. Hover one to read what it does.
Only your Construction Vehicle builds: select it, open Build, place a Barracks, then a War Factory. Shift queues more.
Pull damaged units back instead of losing them. Survivors gain rank and fight better.
Infantry can garrison city buildings and turn them into strongholds.
Every nation has its own special unit and its own strike power. Check the sidebar.

US.q: In war there is no substitute for victory.
Wars may be fought with weapons, but they are won by men. It is the spirit of the men who follow and of the man who leads that gains the victory.
I propose to fight it out on this line if it takes all summer.
US.a: Ulysses S. Grant, dispatch from Spotsylvania, 1864

US.q: These are the times that try men's souls.
To be prepared for war is one of the most effectual means of preserving peace.
US.a: George Washington, first annual address to Congress, 1790
Brig. Gen. Anthony McAuliffe, reply to the German surrender demand at Bastogne, 1944

TR.q: Armies! Your first objective is the Mediterranean. Forward!
TR.a: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, order of 1 September 1922

TR.q: I do not order you to attack. I order you to die. In the time it takes us to die, other troops and commanders can come and take our places.
TR.o: Ben size taarruzu emretmiyorum, ölmeyi emrediyorum.

TR.q: There is no line of defense, there is a surface of defense. That surface is the whole homeland.
TR.a: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk, Battle of Sakarya, 1921
TR.o: Hatt-ı müdafaa yoktur, sath-ı müdafaa vardır. O satıh bütün vatandır.

TR.q: Peace at home, peace in the world.

IL.q: A time to love, and a time to hate; a time of war, and a time of peace.
IL.o: עֵת לֶאֱהֹב וְעֵת לִשְׂנֹא, עֵת מִלְחָמָה וְעֵת שָׁלוֹם

IL.q: We shall fight the war as if there were no White Paper, and the White Paper as if there were no war.
We are a generation of settlement, and without the steel helmet and the cannon's muzzle we will not be able to plant a tree and build a house.
IL.a: Moshe Dayan, eulogy for Roi Rotberg, 1956

FR.q: France has lost a battle! But France has not lost the war!
FR.o: La France a perdu une bataille ! Mais la France n'a pas perdu la guerre !
De l'audace, encore de l'audace, toujours de l'audace !

DE.q: Whoever fights monsters should see to it that in the process he does not become a monster.
DE.o: Wer mit Ungeheuern kämpft, mag zusehen, dass er nicht dabei zum Ungeheuer wird.

EU.q: We shall fight on the beaches, we shall fight on the landing grounds, we shall fight in the fields and in the streets, we shall fight in the hills; we shall never surrender.
EU.a: Winston Churchill, House of Commons, 4 June 1940

EU.q: Never in the field of human conflict was so much owed by so many to so few.
EU.a: Winston Churchill, House of Commons, 20 August 1940

EU.q: War is merely the continuation of policy by other means.
EU.o: Der Krieg ist eine bloße Fortsetzung der Politik mit anderen Mitteln.

EU.q: Everything in war is very simple, but the simplest thing is difficult.
EU.o: Es ist im Kriege alles sehr einfach, aber das Einfachste ist schwierig.

EU.q: Let him who desires peace prepare for war.
EU.a: Vegetius, Epitoma rei militaris, Book III
EU.o: Igitur qui desiderat pacem, praeparet bellum.

EU.q: In war, three quarters turns on morale; the balance of manpower and materiel counts only for the remaining quarter.
EU.o: À la guerre, les trois quarts sont des affaires morales ; la balance des forces réelles n'est que pour un autre quart.

EU.q: Whatever happens, the flame of French resistance must not and shall not die.
EU.a: Charles de Gaulle, Appeal of 18 June 1940
EU.o: Quoi qu'il arrive, la flamme de la résistance française ne doit pas s'éteindre et ne s'éteindra pas.

EU.q: Nothing except a battle lost can be half so melancholy as a battle won.
EU.a: The Duke of Wellington, after Waterloo, 1815

UA.q: Bury me, then rise up and break your heavy chains.
Soul and body we shall lay down for our freedom.
UA.a: Pavlo Chubynsky, "Ukraine Has Not Yet Perished", 1862
UA.o: Душу й тіло ми положим за нашу свободу

UA.q: The eternal revolutionary: the spirit that drives the body into battle.
UA.o: Вічний революцьонер — дух, що тіло рве до бою

UA.q: Glory to Ukraine! Glory to the heroes!

RU.q: Hard in training, easy on the march.
RU.a: Alexander Suvorov, The Science of Victory
RU.o: Тяжело в ученье — легко в походе.

RU.q: The bullet is a fool, the bayonet a fine fellow.
RU.a: Alexander Suvorov, The Science of Victory

RU.q: Our cause is just. The enemy will be defeated. Victory will be ours.
RU.o: Наше дело правое. Враг будет разбит. Победа будет за нами.

RU.q: Whoever comes to us with the sword shall perish by the sword.
RU.o: Кто с мечом к нам придёт, от меча и погибнет.

IR.q: I see death as nothing but happiness, and life with oppressors as nothing but misery.
IR.a: Imam Hussein ibn Ali, on the road to Karbala, 680
IR.o: إني لا أرى الموت إلا سعادة، ولا الحياة مع الظالمين إلا برما

IR.q: Mountains may move, but you must not. Grit your teeth. Lend your skull to God. Plant your feet firmly in the earth.
IR.a: Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib, to his son at the Battle of the Camel, Nahj al-Balagha, Sermon 11
IR.o: تَزُولُ الْجِبَالُ وَلَا تَزُلْ، عَضَّ عَلَى نَاجِذِكَ، أَعِرِ اللَّهَ جُمْجُمَتَكَ، تِدْ فِي الْأَرْضِ قَدَمَكَ

IR.q: Mighty is he who is wise.
IR.o: توانا بود هر که دانا بود

IR.q: Death lies in living as the conquered, and life lies in dying as the victors.
IR.a: Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib, at Siffin, Nahj al-Balagha, Sermon 51
IR.o: فَالْمَوْتُ فِي حَيَاتِكُمْ مَقْهُورِينَ، وَالْحَيَاةُ فِي مَوْتِكُمْ قَاهِرِينَ

RS.a: Pledge of the mourners of Karbala

RS.q: Plot your plots, strive your utmost, spare no effort: by God, you will never erase our remembrance.
RS.a: Sayyida Zaynab bint Ali, to Yazid in Damascus, 680
RS.o: فكِدْ كيدك، واسعَ سعيك، وناصب جهدك، فوالله لا تمحو ذكرنا

RS.q: If the religion of Muhammad stands only by my death, then, O swords, take me!
RS.a: Shaykh Muhsin Abu al-Hab, in the voice of Imam Hussein
RS.o: إن كان دين محمد لم يستقم إلا بقتلي فيا سيوف خذيني

RS.q: Death lies in living as the conquered, and life lies in dying as the victors.
RS.a: Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib, at Siffin, Nahj al-Balagha, Sermon 51
RS.o: فَالْمَوْتُ فِي حَيَاتِكُمْ مَقْهُورِينَ، وَالْحَيَاةُ فِي مَوْتِكُمْ قَاهِرِينَ

RS.q: I am the son of Mecca and Mina; I am the son of Zamzam and Safa.
RS.a: Imam Ali Zayn al-Abidin (al-Sajjad), sermon in Damascus, 680
RS.o: أنا ابن مكة ومنى، أنا ابن زمزم والصفا

DW.q: I did not rise out of arrogance or vanity, nor to spread corruption or oppression. I rose to seek reform in the nation of my grandfather.
DW.o: إني لم أخرج أشِرًا ولا بطِرًا ولا مفسدًا ولا ظالمًا، وإنما خرجت لطلب الإصلاح في أمة جدي

DW.q: By God, never was a people attacked in the heart of their homes but they were humiliated.
DW.a: Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha, Sermon 27
DW.o: فَوَاللَّهِ مَا غُزِيَ قَوْمٌ قَطُّ فِي عُقْرِ دَارِهِمْ إِلَّا ذَلُّوا

DW.q: Opportunity passes like the passing of clouds.
DW.a: Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha, Saying 21
Sayyida Zaynab bint Ali, to Ibn Ziyad in Kufa, 680

SA.q: I have come to you with men who love death as you love life.
SA.a: Khalid ibn al-Walid, letter to the Persian commanders, 633
SA.o: جئتكم بقوم يحبون الموت كما تحبون الحياة

SA.q: The horse, the night and the desert know me; and the sword, the lance, the paper and the pen.
SA.o: الخيل والليل والبيداء تعرفني، والسيف والرمح والقرطاس والقلم

SA.q: Do not kill a child, a woman or an old man. Do not cut down fruit-bearing trees, and do not destroy a dwelling.
SA.a: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, orders to the army marching to Syria, 634

AE.q: When you see the lion's fangs bared, do not think the lion is smiling.
AE.o: إذا رأيتَ نُيوبَ اللّيثِ بارِزَةً فَلا تَظُنّنّ أنّ اللّيثَ يَبْتَسِمُ

AE.q: Great resolves come in the measure of the resolute.
AE.o: على قَدْرِ أهْلِ العَزْمِ تأتي العَزائِمُ

AE.q: I have come to you with men who love death as you love life.
AE.a: Khalid ibn al-Walid, letter to the Persian commanders, 633
AE.o: جئتكم بقوم يحبون الموت كما تحبون الحياة

AE.q: Do not kill a child, a woman or an old man. Do not cut down fruit-bearing trees, and do not destroy a dwelling.
AE.a: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, orders to the army marching to Syria, 634

PK.q: There is no power on earth that can undo Pakistan.
You are a falcon: flight is your calling. There are other skies before you.
PK.o: تو شاہیں ہے، پرواز ہے کام تیرا — ترے سامنے آسماں اور بھی ہیں

PK.q: Raise your selfhood so high that before every decree, God Himself asks you: tell me, what is your will?
PK.o: خودی کو کر بلند اتنا کہ ہر تقدیر سے پہلے — خدا بندے سے خود پوچھے بتا تیری رضا کیا ہے

IN.q: Slain, you will win heaven; victorious, you will enjoy the earth. So rise, son of Kunti, resolved to fight.
IN.o: हतो वा प्राप्स्यसि स्वर्गं जित्वा वा भोक्ष्यसे महीम्। तस्मादुत्तिष्ठ कौन्तेय युद्धाय कृतनिश्चयः॥

IN.q: You have a right to your actions, but never to their fruits.
An arrow shot by an archer may kill one man or may not; but intellect applied by a wise man can kill even those in the womb.

CN.q: Know the enemy and know yourself; in a hundred battles you will never be in peril.
CN.a: Sun Tzu, The Art of War

CN.q: All warfare is based on deception.
CN.a: Sun Tzu, The Art of War

CN.q: To subdue the enemy without fighting is the supreme excellence.
CN.a: Sun Tzu, The Art of War
CN.o: 不战而屈人之兵，善之善者也

CN.q: Swift as the wind, silent as the forest, fierce as fire, immovable as the mountain.
CN.a: Sun Tzu, The Art of War
CN.o: 其疾如风，其徐如林，侵掠如火，不动如山

CN.q: In war, let your great object be victory, not lengthy campaigns.
CN.a: Sun Tzu, The Art of War

CN.q: Political power grows out of the barrel of a gun.

KP.q: Your divine plans have plumbed the heavens; your subtle reckoning has spanned the earth. You have won every battle and your merit is great. Now be content, and stop.
KP.a: General Eulji Mundeok, poem to the Sui general Yu Zhongwen, 612
KP.o: 神策究天文 妙算窮地理 戰勝功旣高 知足願云止

KP.q: Seeing profit, think of what is right; seeing danger, offer your life.
KP.a: Ahn Jung-geun, calligraphy written in prison, 1910
KP.o: 見利思義 見危授命

KP.q: Even if the sky falls, there is a hole to rise through.
Even a sheet of paper is lighter when two lift it together.

KR.q: Those who seek to die shall live; those who seek to live shall die.
KR.a: Admiral Yi Sun-sin, before the Battle of Myeongnyang, 1597
KR.o: 必死則生 必生則死

KR.q: Your servant still has twelve warships.
KR.a: Admiral Yi Sun-sin, report to King Seonjo, 1597
KR.o: 今臣戰船 尙有十二

KR.q: One man holding a narrow pass can strike fear into a thousand.
KR.o: 一夫當逕 足懼千夫

KR.q: The battle is at its height. Do not announce my death.
KR.a: Admiral Yi Sun-sin, Battle of Noryang, 1598
KR.o: 戰方急 愼勿言我死

KR.q: To give one's life for one's country is the duty of a soldier.
KR.a: Ahn Jung-geun, calligraphy written in prison, 1910
KR.o: 爲國獻身 軍人本分

EG.q: What was taken by force can only be restored by force.
EG.o: ما أُخذ بالقوة لا يُسترد بغير القوة

EG.q: Goals are not won by wishing; the world is taken by struggle.
EG.o: وما نيلُ المطالبِ بالتمنّي، ولكن تؤخَذُ الدنيا غِلابا

EG.q: All creation stood watching how I alone lay the foundations of glory.
EG.o: وقف الخلقُ ينظرون جميعًا كيف أبني قواعدَ المجدِ وحدي

EG.q: I have come to you with men who love death as you love life.
EG.a: Khalid ibn al-Walid, letter to the Persian commanders, 633
EG.o: جئتكم بقوم يحبون الموت كما تحبون الحياة

CU.q: Trenches of ideas are worth more than trenches of stone.
CU.o: Trincheras de ideas valen más que trincheras de piedra.

CU.q: To die for the homeland is to live.
CU.o: Morir por la patria es vivir.

CU.q: Whoever tries to seize Cuba will gather only the dust of her soil drenched in blood, if he does not perish in the struggle.
CU.o: Quien intente apropiarse de Cuba recogerá el polvo de su suelo anegado en sangre, si no perece en la lucha.

GB.q: We shall defend our island, whatever the cost may be. We shall never surrender.
GB.a: Winston Churchill, House of Commons, 4 June 1940

GB.q: Never in the field of human conflict was so much owed by so many to so few.
GB.a: Winston Churchill, House of Commons, 20 August 1940

GB.q: England expects that every man will do his duty.
GB.a: Admiral Horatio Nelson, signal at Trafalgar, 1805
Motto of the Special Air Service

GB.q: Nothing except a battle lost can be half so melancholy as a battle won.
GB.a: The Duke of Wellington, after Waterloo, 1815

JP.q: The fate of the Empire rests on this battle; let every man do his utmost.
JP.o: 皇国ノ興廃此ノ一戦ニ在リ、各員一層奮励努力セヨ

JP.q: Do nothing that is of no use.
JP.a: Miyamoto Musashi, The Book of Five Rings, 1645
JP.o: 役に立たぬ事をせざる事

JP.q: Fall seven times, stand up eight.
After victory, tighten the strings of your helmet.
JP.o: 勝って兜の緒を締めよ

RV.q: Do not be the slave of another, when God has made you free.
RV.a: Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha
RV.o: لا تكن عبد غيرك وقد جعلك الله حرًّا

RV.a: Imam Ali to his son at the Battle of the Camel, 656
RV.o: تزول الجبال ولا تزل، أعر الله جمجمتك، تِد في الأرض قدمك

RV.q: Patience is to faith what the head is to the body.
RV.a: Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib, Nahj al-Balagha
RV.o: الصبر من الإيمان بمنزلة الرأس من الجسد

OB.o: على هذه الأرض ما يستحق الحياة

OB.q: Here we shall stay, like a wall upon your chest.
Fighting is prescribed for you, though you dislike it; perhaps you dislike a thing and it is good for you.
OB.o: كُتِبَ عَلَيْكُمُ الْقِتَالُ وَهُوَ كُرْهٌ لَّكُمْ ۖ وَعَسَىٰ أَن تَكْرَهُوا شَيْئًا وَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَّكُمْ

value: Test range now opens a small window: choose your nation, the target nation (it can be the same one) and a map, then Start. Inside the range, "Change nations…" in the Test range box restarts it with a new pair, no trip through the main menu.

Build a Generator (Build tab, about the price of a Barracks) to power your electronic buildings: air defense, coastal missiles, the Strike Center, Radio & TV, the Airfield and your minimap radar. Your top bar shows power produced and used: green is fine, red means LOW POWER and those buildings go offline until you build another Generator or capture a map power plant. Barracks, War Factory, Depot and defense guns never need power. Blowing up enemy Generators is a real tactic.
Every building has its own queue

Like Generals: infantry come only from a Barracks, vehicles from a War Factory, aircraft from an Airfield, ships from a Shipyard. Select the building to see what it can make and its own queue (progress bar on the first unit, ×3 badges). Click = add one, Shift+click = add five, right-click a queued icon = cancel one with a full refund. Two Barracks build two soldiers at the same time; each unit walks out of its own building to that building's rally point. With nothing selected the Units tab still works and picks the least busy building. A destroyed building refunds its queue. The old +50% speed for a second building is gone.
One game: Battle, now with supply lines

The game is now one game: Battle (Command Center, supply trucks, tech tree, destroy every enemy building). Conquest and the Grand campaign are gone. Battle has SUPPLY LINES: the roads running out of your Command Center and Supply Depots are green on the minimap (L shows them on the ground). Units refill ammo near your buildings and on those roads; far beyond them they fight until empty, then must come back or get an Ammo Truck from the War Factory. Craters, blown bridges and enemy checkpoints cut a line (dashed) - your Construction Vehicle repairs a crater fast. Every old battlefield is now a Battle map, and the main menu is Play · Multiplayer · Test range.
The main menu shows your war
The main menu background now shows whatever Continue would take you back to: that battlefield with your front line drawn in.
Every button says what it beats

Unit buttons now carry two small pictures: green = what this unit BEATS best, red = what it is most WEAK TO. Hold the mouse on a button for the full list with names. Point at an enemy unit (or select it) and the buttons that beat it light up green with "BEATS IT". The game works these out from the real damage, armor, range and price numbers against the nation you are fighting, so they are always true - the Encyclopedia and the Unit guide show the same.

Every report from the field - base under attack, enemy spotted, unit lost, building finished, a unit ready - is now one short line with a small icon at the top left of the battle (three lines at most, each fades after a few seconds). Lines marked with a small arrow know where it happened: click the line, or press Space, and the camera goes there. Settings has a switch for it.

When something happens away from where you are looking - your base or troops come under attack, a unit is lost, a unit or building is finished, a teammate pings the map - a small round marker with an arrow now sits on the edge of the screen pointing at it for about six seconds (three at most). Click it and the camera goes there. Settings has a switch for it.

The sound is mixed properly now: even the biggest fight no longer crackles or distorts, unit voices stay clear over the guns (explosions and music step back a little while a soldier speaks), every button and menu item gives a soft click, and each battlefield has a quiet background of its own - dry desert wind, wind in the trees, or a thin winter howl - with the muffled thump of fighting elsewhere on the map.

Every nation now fights with one of four styles: Zealous (slow to break, banners rally the faithful, heavier losses), Professional (steady under artillery, rally fast near officers), Home defenders (much braver on home turf) and Firepower-reliant (break sooner, but stronger fire support). The style shows on the nation pick screen and in the Encyclopedia.

value.inf: Rifle squads are the backbone of any army. Trained to fight from cover, they take ground, garrison buildings and screen the armor. They are cheap, flexible and decisive in towns and broken terrain, and very vulnerable in the open.
value.at: Anti-tank teams carry shoulder-fired or tripod-mounted guided missiles and rockets that can kill an armored vehicle from ambush. Modern infantry relies on them to stop tanks that would otherwise run it down.
value.hacker: Electronic-warfare and cyber specialists disrupt enemy sensors, radios and networks. Armies keep small teams near the front to blind or disable equipment rather than to destroy it.
value.hero: A marksman or sniper team: a trained shooter and a spotter pick off officers and crews from long range, using concealment rather than firepower.
value.champ: Elite special forces are small, highly trained units used for raids, ambushes and high-value-target operations. They are expensive and few, and punch far above their numbers.
value.cleric: A respected religious or political figure whose presence steadies the troops around him. Morale, belief and cohesion matter in combat as much as weapons do. The Ayatollah (Iran, Hezbollah, Ansarallah): Steadfast (infantry near him recover from suppression twice as fast, take 15% less artillery and air damage), Path of Hussein (a fallen soldier near him raises a green banner for 20 s; comrades nearby hit 8% harder, up to 3), Sermon (120 s: a green halo, +20% fire rate, +15% speed and no suppression for 25 s) and Call to Arms (300 s: 6 volunteer riflemen at him and at each barracks). The Dear Leader (North Korea): On-the-spot guidance (a production building beside him builds 25% faster, artillery near him reloads 15% faster), Unbreakable Spirit (wounded units near him keep full damage and speed; damaged vehicles mend slowly), Supreme Commander's Order (120 s: every artillery and rocket unit near him fires one free volley at a chosen spot, then fires faster and farther for 25 s) and Mass Mobilization (300 s: infantry train 50% faster and 25% cheaper for 20 s, and 8 Worker-Peasant Guards form at each barracks). Press E for the ability, Shift+E for the ultimate. If he falls: mourning, +15% damage for 40 s, and a new one can be chosen after 3 minutes.
value.tank: Main battle tanks combine a stabilized high-velocity gun, thick composite armor and a powerful engine. They lead armored assaults and break enemy lines, but need infantry and air-defence cover in towns and against anti-tank missiles.
value.arty: Self-propelled guns and rocket launchers shell targets many kilometers away, then move before counter-battery fire arrives. Superb against massed troops and buildings, nearly helpless once the enemy reaches them.
value.aa: Mobile air-defence vehicles carry radar-guided guns or short-range missiles to protect columns and bases from helicopters, jets and drones.
value.ammot: Ammo trucks follow the army: they top up the ammunition of friendly units close to them, carry a limited stock and reload inside your own area. Light armor, no weapon: keep them behind the front.
value.harv: Supply trucks are the logistics backbone: fuel, ammunition and food move by road. Armies lose more equipment to broken supply than to enemy fire.
value.dozer: Combat engineers build bridges, fortifications and camps and clear obstacles, often under fire. The heavy construction vehicle is how an army digs in and builds forward. Right-click fallen-building rubble with one to clear the way for tanks and supply trucks.
value.heli: Attack helicopters hunt armor from behind hills and tree lines with guided missiles and cannon. Fast and flexible, they are vulnerable to air defense and massed small-arms fire.
value.jet: Strike fighters and fighter-bombers drop precision-guided bombs and fire missiles at targets far behind the line, then leave before air defenses can react.
value.drone: Armed strike drones and loitering munitions turned small, cheap aircraft into precision weapons: they find a target, circle, and dive onto it.
value.boat: Fast attack craft and patrol boats guard coasts and shipping lanes with guns and anti-ship missiles, using speed instead of armor.
value.sub: Submarines hunt ships quietly and strike with torpedoes or missiles from beneath the surface. Their greatest weapon is not being found.
value.ship: Destroyers and frigates are the workhorses of the surface fleet: radar, missiles and guns protect task forces and shell coastlines.
value.lander: Landing craft carry vehicles and troops from ship to beach, the slow, exposed link in any amphibious assault.
value.airlift: Transport aircraft and heavy helicopters move troops and equipment quickly across terrain blocked by rivers, mountains or enemy fire.

value.hq: The command headquarters is the heart of an army's base: planning, communications and the engineers who build everything else. Lose it and the rest of the base is soon lost.
value.barracks: Barracks house, train and equip infantry. Real armies train recruits in camps like this, then rotate squads to the front.
value.factory: The War Factory stands for the vehicle depots and armor plants that build, repair and refit tanks, trucks and artillery.
value.airfield: Airfields give aircraft and drones a runway, hangars, fuel and maintenance crews. A jet is only useful as long as its base survives.
value.shipyard: The shipyard builds, repairs and launches naval vessels. It must sit on the coast, which makes it an obvious target.
value.turret: Fixed gun positions cover approaches and chokepoints. Real defense lines combine such guns with mines, wire and observers.
value.sam: Surface-to-air missile sites guard cities and bases from jets and helicopters, often with a radar nearby to cue the launchers.
value.coast: Coastal missile batteries deny the sea near a shoreline to enemy ships, hiding mobile launchers among the hills and ports.
value.tunnel: Tunnel networks let a defender hide, move and resupply under the enemy's air power, a method used by many armies in mountains and hills.
value.uplink: The Strike Center stands for the long-range missile and air-strike commands that plan and launch deep attacks far behind the front.
value.depot: A forward supply depot stores fuel and ammunition near the fighting so trucks do not need to drive back to the main base.
value.fort: A mountain fortress is a hardened position dug into rock, built to survive bombardment and to hold a pass for a long time.
value.econ: Civil and commercial offices that keep an economy running during a war.
